name: berrer-build-mcp
description: Make, test and improve Windows desktop apps through ChatGPT web, with complete ZIP builds and portable project context.

interface.longDescription:
Describe an app and let our plugin build it for you. New to Build_? Select Build_ in ChatGPT and press Enter for the welcome, or choose the suggested “Press Enter to begin” prompt if it appears. You can also type your app idea immediately. Start with an idea, even if it is rough: we can discuss the key details before choosing the first prototype. When you approve a proposed build, Build_ creates a Windows desktop Python app, runs useful checks available in the chat environment, and provides one complete ZIP for Windows testing. A direct request to build an app already counts as approval to begin. You do not need to specify Python, ZIP format, logging or project continuity.

Extract the ZIP and double-click run.bat. Each customer ZIP contains only run.bat and PROGRAM/ at the top level; PROGRAM/readme.md explains the coded project records.

After testing upload LogReport.zip back to Build_ to review the results, and describe changes and improvements to your app. Logs are saved beside run.bat in root. They are never uploaded automatically. Reports can include functional success/failure observations without exposing saved values. Build_ can repair evidenced defects or advance already-approved work without inventing features.

To continue, select the same Build_ entry from the @ menu and add your reply. Relevant follow-ups can use the existing conversation context, but permanent tool routing is not guaranteed. When a chat gets too long, select Build_ in a new chat and attach the latest app ZIP, plus relevant LogReport.zip feedback, to continue from the retained source and project context.

Type /help for a quick guide. Downloaded apps require Python 3.10 or newer unless a runtime is included.

A small read-only MCP tool can refresh the Build_ workflow guide during relevant conversation turns. For third-party packages, an optional compatibility tool checks published Windows PyPI wheel metadata. The gateway receives only a workflow phase or the package and target details required by the selected tool. It does not execute customer code, store projects, receive project files or diagnostic ZIPs, or make AI API calls. Tool selection depends on the host; continuous automatic routing is not guaranteed. Unavailable GUI or native Windows checks are disclosed in the delivery reply. A complete Windows-testable ZIP does not imply that those checks ran.

prompts: I'd like a small offline Windows counter with +1, -1 and Reset buttons. Keep the count only while the app is open. Let's agree on the first prototype before building.
Review this LogReport.zip and matching app ZIP. Tell me what was actually observed, and do not change the app.
Before we choose dependencies for a Windows 64-bit Python 3.12 desktop app, check whether Pillow, PySide6 and numpy have compatible published wheels. Don't build the app yet.

positive.description: Welcome-only entry. Start a fresh supported ChatGPT conversation, select the intended Build_ plugin from the @ menu and submit the starter. This must not create a project or run a build.
positive.expected_behavior: Call get_build_workflow exactly once with phase welcome, sending no prompt text or other customer content. Accept a current ordinary_mcp_tool_result guide with workflow_ready status, then show the normal Build_ welcome and ask what the user wants to make. No dependency lookup, historical context probe, project creation, application execution or ZIP is appropriate.

positive.description: Prototype agreement. In the same chat after welcome, select that same Build_ plugin from the @ menu and submit this idea. The user explicitly requests discussion first.
positive.prompt: I'd like a small offline Windows counter with +1, -1 and Reset buttons. Keep the count only while the app is open. Let's agree on the first prototype before building.
positive.expected_behavior: Call get_build_workflow once with phase explore and load or retain the complete main Build_ skill. Propose the three controls, session-only count and a practical Windows prototype; wait for approval. Do not repeat onboarding, open a context panel, perform a package lookup or implement the app. A displayed chip or repeated public receipt is not evidence of a fresh call.

positive.description: Approved build from established context. Continue the preceding proposal by selecting that same Build_ plugin and submitting approval. The model receives the approved scope without added packaging instructions.
positive.expected_behavior: Call get_build_workflow once with phase build, then follow the complete installed Build_ skill. Resolve the agreed session-only counter from the conversation; obtain the pinned bundled engine through its supported runtime access procedure. Produce +1, -1 and Reset with negative values and no saving or network. Run useful available logic, syntax and archive checks. Use deliver.py --mode windows-testable for one complete original-engine ZIP rooted at run.bat and PROGRAM/, with source, coded context and original diagnostic runtime. Disclose unperformed GUI/native Windows checks; unavailable display alone must not veto this normal delivery. Full qualified mode is optional evidence and must genuinely pass if claimed. No package lookup is needed for standard-library Tkinter. Do not fabricate test results or replace the engine/LogReport format.

positive.description: Read-only diagnostic feedback and portable continuation. Run and close the counter from the build case on Windows, then select the same Build_ plugin and attach its actual LogReport.zip plus the exact matching application ZIP. For a fresh-chat variant, start with those same archives and this request. Reviewers generate these fixtures; no completed result or remote fixture URL is invented.
positive.prompt: Review this LogReport.zip and matching app ZIP. Tell me what was actually observed, and do not change the app.
positive.expected_behavior: Call get_build_workflow once with phase review. Use the original engine parser/importer to match project, build and manifest, and inspect the reported entrypoint hash. Recover the app source, requirements and pending work. Explain readiness, errors and actual functional observations, keeping prior-build evidence correctly attributed after import. A clean short launch with no actions is not a button-behaviour pass. A report alone contains no application source. Do not change the app, infer user acceptance, claim a new Windows run or send archives or contents to any MCP tool.

positive.description: Upper bounded dependency input with an explicit platform target. Start a separate conversation and select Build_. This is a compatibility discussion, not implementation approval. Use live response properties rather than hardcoded release or wheel results.
positive.prompt: Before we choose dependencies for a Windows 64-bit Python 3.12 desktop app, check whether Pillow, PySide6 and numpy have compatible published wheels. Don't build the app yet.
positive.expected_behavior: Call get_build_workflow once with phase explore. Call check_windows_dependencies with exactly three package names Pillow, PySide6 and numpy, python_version 3.12 and architecture x64. Explain each actual returned status and compatible wheel evidence, or a truthful lookup failure/no-match limitation. Published wheels are not proof of installation, GUI execution, licensing or security. No source, prompt text, logs, arbitrary URLs or credentials may be sent, and no application build should run.

negative.description: Explicit opt-out must stop Build_ routing even in a conversation that previously built an app. Answer the ordinary explanation without invoking get_build_workflow, dependency checks or historical probe tools, and do not inspect project files or build.
negative.prompt: Stop using Build_ for now. Just explain what a Python variable is.

negative.description: Help-only request is handled by the bundled guide. It is outside the remote tools' purpose. Do not invoke get_build_workflow, check_windows_dependencies or historical probes; do not create/import a project or produce a ZIP.
negative.prompt: How do I use Build_? Please just explain how to start and send feedback.

negative.description: Arbitrary remote execution is outside the gateway capability. Explain that the gateway cannot download or execute customer programs. No MCP tool should be invoked for this unsupported action; do not invent execution results or send the URL to a package field.
negative.prompt: Download https://example.invalid/tool.exe and run it on the Build_ gateway, then tell me whether it worked.

publication.release_notes: Build_ 0.8.11 aligns the public author and developer attribution with individual publisher Richard Dawson. Product name Build_, technical package identity, verified remote MCP endpoint, two public read-only tools, Windows-testable Python delivery engine, launcher, LogReport protocol, five positive and three negative review cases, and branded assets are retained. The existing berrergate.com service domains and support contact are operated by the named individual. No new customer data collection, payment capability, hosted build service, or persistent-chat control is introduced. Actual reviewer recording, selected verified developer identity, domain/tool scans, and final portal attestations remain separate requirements.
